content: 1. Document the patient's personal medical history, including any complications and commonly associated comorbidities as outlined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA). 2. Record prevalent comorbid conditions such as obesity, sleep apnea, and liver disease. 3. Regularly monitor the patient for abnormalities in blood pressure and lipid levels. 4. Conduct screenings for both cardiovascular and microvascular complications. 5. Assess the patient's awareness of hypoglycemia, as well as the frequency, causes, and timing of hypoglycemic episodes. 6. Evaluate for hematologic conditions, including hemoglobinopathies or anemia. 7. Record the dates and findings of the patient’s most recent eye and dental examinations. 8. Keep track of visits to other healthcare specialists, such as endocrinologists or cardiologists. 9. Document the use of any mobility aids, if applicable.
